_comment: Multipart, for the same reason the composter's is: the tub is one part that is always drawn and
the contents are a single quad over it. As variants, every level would be a full copy of the
`filled` is what chooses the PROCESS, so it also chooses what the contents look like. Dry, you
watch a heap of kief pile up on the screen exactly as before. Filled, all you see is the water:
the resin is underneath it, where you genuinely could not see it, so the levels deliberately
look identical and the composter's fill sound is the progress feedback (a comparator gives the
exact number for anyone who wants one).
Level 8 is the batch waiting to be taken, and it is the one state that must read differently in
each mode -- kief heaped to the rim when dry, washed powder sitting proud of the water when wet.
Multipart ANDs the keys in a single `when`, which is what makes that expressible without a
second property: the water is deliberately not spent until collection precisely so that this
state still remembers which process made it.
Heights follow vanilla's composter exactly (3,5,7,9,11,13,15) so the fill reads at the rate
players already know from a block that looks like this one.
